chunks.title: HAAD Clinical Laboratory Standards
chunks.issuer: Health Authority Abu Dhabi (HAAD) — now Department of Health (DoH) Abu Dhabi
chunks.publication_date: not stated in document (PDF creation metadata 2011-05-22)
chunks.applicability: Applies to licensed clinical laboratories in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi. For an AE-DU case this is an OUT-OF-JURISDICTION COMPARATOR only.
chunks.text: The director has defined in writing, a procedure for immediate notification of the responsible clinician when specific critical results indicate that the patient's situation is life-threatening.
chunks.support_note: Abu Dhabi requires an immediate-notification procedure aimed at a responsible clinician - a different recipient model from DHA's walk-in patient. Comparability only.

chunks.title: HAAD Clinical Laboratory Standards
chunks.issuer: Health Authority Abu Dhabi (HAAD) — now Department of Health (DoH) Abu Dhabi
chunks.publication_date: not stated in document (PDF creation metadata 2011-05-22)
chunks.applicability: Applies to licensed clinical laboratories in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi. For an AE-DU case this is an OUT-OF-JURISDICTION COMPARATOR only.
chunks.text: The means of notifying the clinician of these critical values is defined. For inpatients, the process might be notifying a responsible nurse who calls the physician. For outpatients, the response may be to directly notify the physician.
chunks.support_note: Shows a comparator jurisdiction delegating channel choice to the facility rather than mandating a channel.

chunks.title: HAAD Clinical Laboratory Standards
chunks.issuer: Health Authority Abu Dhabi (HAAD) — now Department of Health (DoH) Abu Dhabi
chunks.publication_date: not stated in document (PDF creation metadata 2011-05-22)
chunks.applicability: Applies to licensed clinical laboratories in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi. For an AE-DU case this is an OUT-OF-JURISDICTION COMPARATOR only.
chunks.text: The notification is documented, including time and date called, and the identification of the individual called. This individual should write down and read back the result to ensure that it has been understood
chunks.support_note: The closest comparator evidence for a read-back/understanding concept. Still addresses a clinician recipient, and is written as "should". The sentence continues with the single word "accurately" at the top of page 14; the quotation is truncated here so that it verifies contiguously against the PDF text layer.

chunks.title: HAAD Clinical Laboratory Standards
chunks.issuer: Health Authority Abu Dhabi (HAAD) — now Department of Health (DoH) Abu Dhabi
chunks.publication_date: not stated in document (PDF creation metadata 2011-05-22)
chunks.applicability: Applies to licensed clinical laboratories in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi. For an AE-DU case this is an OUT-OF-JURISDICTION COMPARATOR only.
chunks.text: The laboratory has a written, defined process for correcting reported results, including the following: a) When an incorrect result is reported, the corrected report is generated as promptly as possible.
chunks.support_note: Requires a written correction process with prompt regeneration of the corrected report.

chunks.title: HAAD Clinical Laboratory Standards
chunks.issuer: Health Authority Abu Dhabi (HAAD) — now Department of Health (DoH) Abu Dhabi
chunks.publication_date: not stated in document (PDF creation metadata 2011-05-22)
chunks.applicability: Applies to licensed clinical laboratories in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi. For an AE-DU case this is an OUT-OF-JURISDICTION COMPARATOR only.
chunks.text: b) In such cases, the laboratory communicates directly with the ordering clinician or other authorized qualified individual who can take action to avert maltreatment of the patient.
chunks.support_note: The strongest comparator evidence that a correction triggers its own re-communication duty - stronger than the Dubai instrument retrieved here.

chunks.title: HAAD Clinical Laboratory Standards
chunks.issuer: Health Authority Abu Dhabi (HAAD) — now Department of Health (DoH) Abu Dhabi
chunks.publication_date: not stated in document (PDF creation metadata 2011-05-22)
chunks.applicability: Applies to licensed clinical laboratories in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi. For an AE-DU case this is an OUT-OF-JURISDICTION COMPARATOR only.
chunks.text: c) The process includes maintenance of both the original and corrected reports, with identification of each on all copies of the report.
chunks.support_note: Explicit version-identification requirement for both the original and the correction.

chunks.title: HAAD Clinical Laboratory Standards
chunks.issuer: Health Authority Abu Dhabi (HAAD) — now Department of Health (DoH) Abu Dhabi
chunks.publication_date: not stated in document (PDF creation metadata 2011-05-22)
chunks.applicability: Applies to licensed clinical laboratories in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi. For an AE-DU case this is an OUT-OF-JURISDICTION COMPARATOR only.
chunks.text: The director defines in a written policy requirements for giving or receiving verbal and telephone orders or test results. These include requirements that: a) The complete verbal or telephone order or test result shall be written down legibly and signed by the receiver of the order or test result.
chunks.support_note: Read-back regime exists in policy for verbal results, in the Abu Dhabi instrument.

chunks.title: HAAD Clinical Laboratory Standards
chunks.issuer: Health Authority Abu Dhabi (HAAD) — now Department of Health (DoH) Abu Dhabi
chunks.publication_date: not stated in document (PDF creation metadata 2011-05-22)
chunks.applicability: Applies to licensed clinical laboratories in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi. For an AE-DU case this is an OUT-OF-JURISDICTION COMPARATOR only.
chunks.text: b) The complete verbal and telephone order or test result shall be read back by the receiver of the order or test result.
chunks.support_note: Uses "shall". This is the closest comparator concept to a verified human acknowledgment, and it exists only for verbal/telephone transmission.

chunks.title: AI Ready – Analysis Towards a Standardized Readiness Framework, Report 2.0
chunks.issuer: International Telecommunication Union (ITU)
chunks.applicability: Readiness framework used for mapping only
chunks.text: The AI Policy dimension evaluates the maturity of institutional frameworks essential for trustworthy and responsible AI ecosystems. We selected AI Policy and Regulation, Regulatory Quality, and Implementation as they collectively represent the indispensable triad for accountable AI systems.
chunks.support_note: Verifies the published AI Policy dimension and its three indices. Mapping target for the policy/governance perspective.

chunks.title: AI Ready – Analysis Towards a Standardized Readiness Framework, Report 2.0
chunks.issuer: International Telecommunication Union (ITU)
chunks.applicability: Readiness framework used for mapping only
chunks.text: The Innovation Ecosystem assesses the broader environment that nurtures and accelerates the advancement and adoption of Artificial Intelligence. It focuses on the critical inputs and collaborative dynamics that transform research into tangible progress and practical applications. We examine six key dimensions: standards, Engagement in Open source, R&D, investment, GenAI Content, and AI Technology market size.
chunks.support_note: The only verified anchor for open-source and standards mapping in Report 2.0. Note the published index list here differs slightly from the summary table (which omits GenAI Content) - recorded as a source-internal inconsistency.

chunks.title: AI Ready – Analysis Towards a Standardized Readiness Framework, Report 2.0
chunks.issuer: International Telecommunication Union (ITU)
chunks.applicability: Readiness framework used for mapping only
chunks.text: The Data dimension evaluates foundational data readiness for AI development and deployment.
chunks.support_note: Used to frame provenance-oriented data handling as a readiness-relevant capability, not as a score.

chunks.title: National Patient Safety Goals — Laboratory Program (effective January 2026)
chunks.issuer: The Joint Commission (United States)
chunks.applicability: Applies to Joint Commission-accredited laboratory programmes (not UAE facilities)
chunks.text: Critical results of tests and diagnostic procedures fall significantly outside the normal range and may indicate a life-threatening situation. The objective is to provide the responsible licensed caregiver these results within an established time frame so that the patient can be promptly treated.
chunks.support_note: Comparator states the objective in terms of a responsible licensed caregiver and an organisation-established time frame.

chunks.title: National Patient Safety Goals — Laboratory Program (effective January 2026)
chunks.issuer: The Joint Commission (United States)
chunks.applicability: Applies to Joint Commission-accredited laboratory programmes (not UAE facilities)
chunks.text: Collaborate with organization leaders to develop and implement written procedures for managing the critical results of tests and diagnostic procedures that address the following: • The definition of critical results of tests and diagnostic procedures • By whom and to whom critical results of tests and diagnostic procedures are reported • The acceptable length of time between the availability and reporting of critical results of tests and diagnostic procedures Documentation is required.
chunks.support_note: Important negative finding for the gap register - the comparator does NOT set a numeric time limit; it requires the organisation to define one in writing.

chunks.title: National Patient Safety Goals — Laboratory Program (effective January 2026)
chunks.issuer: The Joint Commission (United States)
chunks.applicability: Applies to Joint Commission-accredited laboratory programmes (not UAE facilities)
chunks.text: Evaluate the timeliness of reporting the critical results of tests and diagnostic procedures.
chunks.support_note: Requires measurement of timeliness, which presupposes recordable timestamps at reporting.

chunks.title: 2025 SAFER Guide: Test Results Reporting and Follow-Up
chunks.issuer: Office of the National Coordinator for Health IT (ONC), United States
chunks.applicability: Applies to US EHR-enabled organisations; used as a comparator for result-tracking safety functions
chunks.text: The EHR is able to track the status of all test-related orders and procedures associated with them (e.g., specimen received and collected; test completed, reported, and acknowledged).
chunks.support_note: Directly supports separating "reported" from "acknowledged" as distinct tracked states. Inline citation markers (e.g. ".10,29") are omitted from the quotation for readability; this is disclosed rather than silently trimmed.

chunks.title: 2025 SAFER Guide: Test Results Reporting and Follow-Up
chunks.issuer: Office of the National Coordinator for Health IT (ONC), United States
chunks.applicability: Applies to US EHR-enabled organisations; used as a comparator for result-tracking safety functions
chunks.text: When test results are changed or amended, the ordering clinician and other clinicians responsible for follow-up are notified electronically, and the changed results and amended flag should be clearly visible in the EHR.
chunks.support_note: Comparator requires a distinct notification event and a visible amended flag for corrections, separate from the original communication. Inline citation marker ".32" omitted.

chunks.title: 2025 SAFER Guide: Test Results Reporting and Follow-Up
chunks.issuer: Office of the National Coordinator for Health IT (ONC), United States
chunks.applicability: Applies to US EHR-enabled organisations; used as a comparator for result-tracking safety functions
chunks.text: For clinically significant changes, the clinicians are also contacted directly.
chunks.support_note: Escalation of a correction to direct contact is conditioned on clinical significance - i.e. the comparator delegates a clinical judgement that ResultRelay must route to a human rather than infer.

chunks.title: 2025 SAFER Guide: Test Results Reporting and Follow-Up
chunks.issuer: Office of the National Coordinator for Health IT (ONC), United States
chunks.applicability: Applies to US EHR-enabled organisations; used as a comparator for result-tracking safety functions
chunks.text: Written policies specify unambiguous responsibility for test result follow-up with a shared understanding of that responsibility among all involved in providing follow-up care.
chunks.support_note: Supports the design choice of a named responsible role rather than an anonymous queue.

chunks.title: HL7 FHIR R5 — Task resource
chunks.issuer: Health Level Seven International (HL7)
chunks.applicability: Interoperability vocabulary for workflow tasks; comparator for state modelling
chunks.text: The assignment of tasks into categories by type of task, type of performer and task status enable the server to function as a queue of work items.
chunks.support_note: FHIR Task models a work item with a status - not delivery of a message nor human acknowledgment of clinical content.

chunks.title: HL7 FHIR R5 — Task resource
chunks.issuer: Health Level Seven International (HL7)
chunks.applicability: Interoperability vocabulary for workflow tasks; comparator for state modelling
chunks.text: draft | requested | received | accepted |
chunks.support_note: The rendered R5 HTML truncates the required binding with "+"; only the first four values appear verbatim and are quoted here, with the remainder of the Task Status value set not asserted. Interpretation (flagged as interpretation, not quote) - "completed" describes the task, not evidence that a human understood a result.

chunks.title: Cross-Enterprise Document Workflow (XDW) content profile
chunks.issuer: IHE International (IT Infrastructure Technical Framework, Vol. 1, Ch. 30)
chunks.applicability: Workflow-document interoperability comparator; comparator only.
chunks.text: This profile defines an instrument, called a "Workflow Document", to manage and track a shared workflow. It records the creation of tasks and maintains a historical record of tasks as they move through the associated workflow.
chunks.support_note: Supports append-only task history and shared workflow state as an interoperability pattern.

chunks.title: Cross-Enterprise Document Workflow (XDW) content profile
chunks.issuer: IHE International (IT Infrastructure Technical Framework, Vol. 1, Ch. 30)
chunks.applicability: Workflow-document interoperability comparator; comparator only.
chunks.text: This actor shall be able to solve "race condition" events
chunks.support_note: Confirms that concurrent workflow updates are a recognised interoperability problem with a defined actor responsibility.

chunks.title: Standards for Clinical Laboratory Services
chunks.issuer: Dubai Health Authority (Health Regulation Sector / Health Policies and Standards Dept)
chunks.applicability: Applies to DHA-licensed clinical laboratories in the Emirate of Dubai
chunks.text: Licensed Clinical Laboratories may accept walk-in patients for specific laboratory tests that do not require a physician's order. Refer to the list of services permitted elaborated in Appendix 3.
chunks.support_note: Establishes that walk-in testing is limited to a permitted list, i.e. a scope boundary exists.

chunks.title: Standards for Clinical Laboratory Services
chunks.issuer: Dubai Health Authority (Health Regulation Sector / Health Policies and Standards Dept)
chunks.applicability: Applies to DHA-licensed clinical laboratories in the Emirate of Dubai
chunks.text: Critical laboratory results shall be reported clearly to the patient.
chunks.support_note: The only walk-in-specific critical-result sentence in the instrument. It does not define delivery, acknowledgment, or timing.

chunks.title: Standards for Clinical Laboratory Services
chunks.issuer: Dubai Health Authority (Health Regulation Sector / Health Policies and Standards Dept)
chunks.applicability: Applies to DHA-licensed clinical laboratories in the Emirate of Dubai
chunks.text: The laboratory should direct the patient to seek further medical advice.
chunks.support_note: Uses "should", not "shall". Classified as guidance, and it is the sourced basis for patient-facing wording.

chunks.title: Standards for Clinical Laboratory Services
chunks.issuer: Dubai Health Authority (Health Regulation Sector / Health Policies and Standards Dept)
chunks.applicability: Applies to DHA-licensed clinical laboratories in the Emirate of Dubai
chunks.text: The laboratory shall keep record of the communication with the patient.
chunks.support_note: Requires a record of the communication. Does not specify what constitutes sufficient evidence of receipt.

chunks.title: Standards for Clinical Laboratory Services
chunks.issuer: Dubai Health Authority (Health Regulation Sector / Health Policies and Standards Dept)
chunks.applicability: Applies to DHA-licensed clinical laboratories in the Emirate of Dubai
chunks.text: The laboratory shall have a policy for identifying and reporting critical results.
chunks.support_note: The instrument delegates mechanism design to the laboratory's own policy - a key point for the gap register.

chunks.title: Standards for Clinical Laboratory Services
chunks.issuer: Dubai Health Authority (Health Regulation Sector / Health Policies and Standards Dept)
chunks.applicability: Applies to DHA-licensed clinical laboratories in the Emirate of Dubai
chunks.text: The laboratory shall ensure that the expected Turn Around Time for each test is well defined in their internal policy.
chunks.support_note: Timing is delegated to internal policy; no numeric clock appears in the instrument itself.

chunks.title: Standards for Clinical Laboratory Services
chunks.issuer: Dubai Health Authority (Health Regulation Sector / Health Policies and Standards Dept)
chunks.applicability: Applies to DHA-licensed clinical laboratories in the Emirate of Dubai
chunks.text: The laboratory shall have a mechanism for correcting erroneous result in a manner that identifies the corrected result as revised and the date and time of correction. Both the original and corrected reports must be maintained and retrievable by the laboratory.
chunks.support_note: Requires a revised identifier, a correction timestamp, and retention of both versions.

chunks.title: Standards for Clinical Laboratory Services
chunks.issuer: Dubai Health Authority (Health Regulation Sector / Health Policies and Standards Dept)
chunks.applicability: Applies to DHA-licensed clinical laboratories in the Emirate of Dubai
chunks.text: Laboratories sending reports electronically should include electronic signature of the authorized signatory. Laboratories should be able to provide critical information required by a physician on telephone.
chunks.support_note: Electronic reporting and integrity of the signatory are addressed; transport delivery semantics are not.

chunks.title: Standards for Clinical Laboratory Services
chunks.issuer: Dubai Health Authority (Health Regulation Sector / Health Policies and Standards Dept)
chunks.applicability: Applies to DHA-licensed clinical laboratories in the Emirate of Dubai
chunks.text: Provisions shall be made for securing electronic laboratory reports.
chunks.support_note: Security obligation exists but is unspecified in detail; carries over to any alternative channel decision.

chunks.title: Standards for Clinical Laboratory Services
chunks.issuer: Dubai Health Authority (Health Regulation Sector / Health Policies and Standards Dept)
chunks.applicability: Applies to DHA-licensed clinical laboratories in the Emirate of Dubai
chunks.text: Patient Result Records and materials shall be retained aligned to the DHA Guidelines for Managing Health Records.
chunks.support_note: Retention is cross-referenced to a separate DHA instrument not reviewed in this build.

chunks.title: Standards for Clinical Laboratory Services
chunks.issuer: Dubai Health Authority (Health Regulation Sector / Health Policies and Standards Dept)
chunks.applicability: Applies to DHA-licensed clinical laboratories in the Emirate of Dubai
chunks.text: A Consultant/Specialist Physician shall be consulted before and after genetic testing.
chunks.support_note: Genetic results carry a distinct clinical pathway requirement.

chunks.title: Standards for Clinical Laboratory Services
chunks.issuer: Dubai Health Authority (Health Regulation Sector / Health Policies and Standards Dept)
chunks.applicability: Applies to DHA-licensed clinical laboratories in the Emirate of Dubai
chunks.text: Genetic results shall not be communicated to the patients directly. The results shall be directed to the referring/treating Physician.
chunks.support_note: Directly contradicts a generic walk-in patient-communication path for genetic results. This is the scope-exclusion anchor for Scenario 3.

chunks.title: Standards for Clinical Laboratory Services
chunks.issuer: Dubai Health Authority (Health Regulation Sector / Health Policies and Standards Dept)
chunks.applicability: Applies to DHA-licensed clinical laboratories in the Emirate of Dubai
chunks.text: Only the referring/treating Physician shall make recommendations or prescribe to the patient any medication or healthcare products, based on the laboratory results.
chunks.support_note: Reinforces that ResultRelay must never interpret or advise treatment.

chunks.title: Standards for Clinical Laboratory Services
chunks.issuer: Dubai Health Authority (Health Regulation Sector / Health Policies and Standards Dept)
chunks.applicability: Applies to DHA-licensed clinical laboratories in the Emirate of Dubai
chunks.text: Genetics All tests under this category requires Prescription
chunks.support_note: Appendix 3 corroborates that genetic testing is not a walk-in permitted category, so §11.1 cannot apply to it.

chunks.title: Federal Law No. (2) of 2019 Concerning the Use of the Information and Communications Technology in Health Fields
chunks.issuer: United Arab Emirates - Federal Government (Ministry of Health and Prevention; official legislation portal)
chunks.document_version: As enacted; Executive Regulation = Cabinet Resolution No. (32) of 2020
chunks.applicability: All health data held, processed or circulated through ICT in the State, expressly including free zones (Article 2). This is the governing instrument for a patient-result-messaging workflow.
chunks.text: To keep the confidentiality of health data and information by not allowing to circulate them in cases other than the permitted.
chunks.support_note: Federal obligation on any ICT use in health fields. "Circulation" is defined in Article 1 to include sending, disclosing and publishing - so a result notification is circulation.

chunks.title: Federal Law No. (2) of 2019 Concerning the Use of the Information and Communications Technology in Health Fields
chunks.issuer: United Arab Emirates - Federal Government (Ministry of Health and Prevention; official legislation portal)
chunks.document_version: As enacted; Executive Regulation = Cabinet Resolution No. (32) of 2020
chunks.applicability: All health data held, processed or circulated through ICT in the State, expressly including free zones (Article 2). This is the governing instrument for a patient-result-messaging workflow.
chunks.text: To ensure the validity and credibility of the health data and information by keeping their safety from the non-authorised damage, amendment, alteration, deletion or addition.
chunks.support_note: Federal basis for the append-only audit log and for revision lineage: amendment must be authorised and attributable, which is what the hash chain and revisions provide.

chunks.title: Federal Law No. (2) of 2019 Concerning the Use of the Information and Communications Technology in Health Fields
chunks.issuer: United Arab Emirates - Federal Government (Ministry of Health and Prevention; official legislation portal)
chunks.document_version: As enacted; Executive Regulation = Cabinet Resolution No. (32) of 2020
chunks.applicability: All health data held, processed or circulated through ICT in the State, expressly including free zones (Article 2). This is the governing instrument for a patient-result-messaging workflow.
chunks.text: It is not permissible to store, process, generate or transform the health data and information outside State -which are related to the health services provided inside State- except in the case where a resolution is issued from the Health Authority in coordination with the Ministry.
chunks.support_note: The clause that makes model placement a compliance question: "process" is listed, so sending health data to an offshore model endpoint is processing outside the State unless a resolution authorises it.

chunks.title: Federal Law No. (2) of 2019 Concerning the Use of the Information and Communications Technology in Health Fields
chunks.issuer: United Arab Emirates - Federal Government (Ministry of Health and Prevention; official legislation portal)
chunks.document_version: As enacted; Executive Regulation = Cabinet Resolution No. (32) of 2020
chunks.applicability: All health data held, processed or circulated through ICT in the State, expressly including free zones (Article 2). This is the governing instrument for a patient-result-messaging workflow.
chunks.text: Without violation to any applicable legislations, whoever circulates information related to the patients must keep its confidentiality and not to use them except in the health purposes without written approval from the patient, except in any of the following cases:
chunks.support_note: Governs circulation of patient information and lists five exceptions (insurers, research, public health, judicial, health-authority inspection). Communicating a result to the patient for health purposes is the permitted path; disclosure to anyone else needs written approval or an exception.

chunks.title: Federal Law No. (2) of 2019 Concerning the Use of the Information and Communications Technology in Health Fields
chunks.issuer: United Arab Emirates - Federal Government (Ministry of Health and Prevention; official legislation portal)
chunks.document_version: As enacted; Executive Regulation = Cabinet Resolution No. (32) of 2020
chunks.applicability: All health data held, processed or circulated through ICT in the State, expressly including free zones (Article 2). This is the governing instrument for a patient-result-messaging workflow.
chunks.text: The keeping period shall commensurate with the need to the health data and information, provided that the keeping period shall not be less than (25) twenty-five years from the last date of the health procedure of the person concerned with such health data and information.
chunks.support_note: A hard retention floor. The prototype stores communication records in a single SQLite file with no retention policy, so this is an open implementation gap (GR-13), not a satisfied requirement.

chunks.title: Federal Law No. (2) of 2019 Concerning the Use of the Information and Communications Technology in Health Fields
chunks.issuer: United Arab Emirates - Federal Government (Ministry of Health and Prevention; official legislation portal)
chunks.document_version: As enacted; Executive Regulation = Cabinet Resolution No. (32) of 2020
chunks.applicability: All health data held, processed or circulated through ICT in the State, expressly including free zones (Article 2). This is the governing instrument for a patient-result-messaging workflow.
chunks.text: Whoever violates the provision of Article (13) of this Law shall be punished of a penalty of no less than (500.000) five hundred thousand dirhams and no more than (700.000) seven hundred thousand dirhams.
chunks.support_note: Quantifies the exposure created by Article 13, which is why the design treats the model endpoint as a governed resource rather than a configuration detail.

chunks.title: Federal Decree-Law No. (45) of 2021 on the Protection of Personal Data (PDPL) - unofficial English translation
chunks.issuer: United Arab Emirates - Federal Government (text); English translation published by Lexis Middle East on a third-party mirror
chunks.document_version: As issued; Executive Regulations not yet issued at retrieval
chunks.applicability: General personal data. Used here ONLY for the scope exclusion in Article 3(e): health personal data subject to legislation regulating its protection and processing falls outside this Decree-Law, which is why the ICT Health Law (U1) governs. PDPL is NOT presented as the applicable health-data instrument.
chunks.text: The provisions of this Decree Law shall not apply to the following: a. government data. b. government authorities that control or process Personal Data. c. Personal Data held with security and judicial authorities. d. a Data Subject who processes his/her data for personal purposes. e. health personal data that is subject to legislation regulating the protection and Processing thereof.
chunks.support_note: The reason a laboratory must not cite PDPL consent mechanics for result notification: health data governed by other legislation is outside this Decree-Law, and in the UAE that legislation is the ICT Health Law (U1). This is the "relevant but not applicable" case the filter exists for.

chunks.title: Federal Decree-Law No. (45) of 2021 on the Protection of Personal Data (PDPL) - unofficial English translation
chunks.issuer: United Arab Emirates - Federal Government (text); English translation published by Lexis Middle East on a third-party mirror
chunks.document_version: As issued; Executive Regulations not yet issued at retrieval
chunks.applicability: General personal data. Used here ONLY for the scope exclusion in Article 3(e): health personal data subject to legislation regulating its protection and processing falls outside this Decree-Law, which is why the ICT Health Law (U1) governs. PDPL is NOT presented as the applicable health-data instrument.
chunks.text: Sensitive Personal Data: Any data that directly or indirectly reveals a natural person's family, racial origin, political or philosophical opinions, religious beliefs, criminal records, biometric data, or any data related to the health of such person, such as his/her physical, psychological, mental, genetic or sexual condition, including information related to health care services provided thereto that reveals his/her health status.
chunks.support_note: Confirms that laboratory results are health data of the most sensitive kind, whichever instrument ultimately governs them. Used to size the handling requirements, not to pick the instrument.

chunks.title: Policy for Health Information Assets Management (HISHD/PP-12)
chunks.issuer: Dubai Health Authority - Health Regulation Sector
chunks.applicability: DHA-licensed health facilities in Dubai. Supplies the operational retention duty that restates the federal 25-year floor.
chunks.text: In general and as per ICT Health Law, HIA must be stored for at least Twenty five (25) years from the date of the last health Procedure/Encounter of the Data Subject/ Patient.
chunks.support_note: Dubai restates the federal 25-year floor as an entity obligation. A communication record is a health information asset, so retention applies to the audit trail and the message log, not only to the laboratory result.

chunks.title: Policy for Health Information Assets Management (HISHD/PP-12)
chunks.issuer: Dubai Health Authority - Health Regulation Sector
chunks.applicability: DHA-licensed health facilities in Dubai. Supplies the operational retention duty that restates the federal 25-year floor.
chunks.text: However, some HIA need more timeline for retention based on business/operational/legal requirements. This decision must be taken by the Entity`s Executive leader/Medical Director with a designated function to appraise HIA.
chunks.support_note: Places the retention decision with a named human role. Supports the design rule that retention and disclosure decisions are institutional, not algorithmic.

chunks.title: Health Data Quality Policy (HISHD/PP-08)
chunks.issuer: Dubai Health Authority - Health Regulation Sector
chunks.applicability: DHA-licensed entities in Dubai. Supplies the accuracy obligation and the patient-feedback duty that a corrected critical result has to satisfy.
chunks.text: Accurate: Data must be accurate and truthful at aggregate and record level, representing what was intended /defined by their official source. Data recorded in Data Subject/Patient EMRs must accurately reflect each other and the care/treatment provided to the Data Subject/Patient.
chunks.support_note: The accuracy obligation a corrected result is meant to restore, and the reason a correction must supersede rather than overwrite: the record has to stay truthful about both versions.

chunks.title: Health Data Quality Policy (HISHD/PP-08)
chunks.issuer: Dubai Health Authority - Health Regulation Sector
chunks.applicability: DHA-licensed entities in Dubai. Supplies the accuracy obligation and the patient-feedback duty that a corrected critical result has to satisfy.
chunks.text: Entities must implement methods to receive patient feedback regarding inaccurate information.
chunks.support_note: A Dubai requirement that the patient can raise an inaccuracy. The prototype has no inbound patient-reporting path: an acknowledgment channel is not a correction channel (GR-14).

chunks.title: The UAE Charter for the Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
chunks.issuer: United Arab Emirates - UAE Council for Artificial Intelligence and Digital Transactions (published on the official legislation portal)
chunks.applicability: National guidance on AI development and use. Voluntary: it defers to sectoral law (Principle 12), so for a health-data workflow it frames design expectations but cannot authorise an action.
chunks.text: The UAE places great importance on safety, ensuring that all AI systems comply with the highest safety standards. The country encourages modifying or removing systems that pose risks.
chunks.support_note: National expectation for AI safety. It is guidance: the gate treats it as a design input that can shape a control, never as a rule that authorises or forbids an action.

chunks.title: The UAE Charter for the Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
chunks.issuer: United Arab Emirates - UAE Council for Artificial Intelligence and Digital Transactions (published on the official legislation portal)
chunks.applicability: National guidance on AI development and use. Voluntary: it defers to sectoral law (Principle 12), so for a health-data workflow it frames design expectations but cannot authorise an action.
chunks.text: The Charter emphasizes the irreplaceable value of human judgment and human oversight over AI, aligning with ethical values and social standards to correct any errors or biases that may arise.
chunks.support_note: The national basis for the architecture decision that a model may propose but a deterministic gate decides: human judgement is described as irreplaceable, not as an optional review layer.

chunks.title: The UAE Charter for the Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
chunks.issuer: United Arab Emirates - UAE Council for Artificial Intelligence and Digital Transactions (published on the official legislation portal)
chunks.applicability: National guidance on AI development and use. Voluntary: it defers to sectoral law (Principle 12), so for a health-data workflow it frames design expectations but cannot authorise an action.
chunks.text: The UAE adopts a responsible and proactive stance, emphasizing the importance of governance and accountability in AI to ensure the technology is used ethically and transparently.
chunks.support_note: Supports the append-only audit trail and the requirement that every consequential action be attributable. Guidance again: the audit trail is a design control, not a quoted obligation.

chunks.title: The UAE Charter for the Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
chunks.issuer: United Arab Emirates - UAE Council for Artificial Intelligence and Digital Transactions (published on the official legislation portal)
chunks.applicability: National guidance on AI development and use. Voluntary: it defers to sectoral law (Principle 12), so for a health-data workflow it frames design expectations but cannot authorise an action.
chunks.text: The UAE seeks to create a clear understanding of AI and how systems operate and make decisions, which helps build trust, enhance responsibility, and accountability in the use of these technologies.
chunks.support_note: The nearest national basis for publishing ordered decision traces (proposal -> gate -> transition -> evidence) rather than an opaque model output.

chunks.title: The UAE Charter for the Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
chunks.issuer: United Arab Emirates - UAE Council for Artificial Intelligence and Digital Transactions (published on the official legislation portal)
chunks.section_id: Principle 12 (Commitment to Treaties and Applicable Laws)
chunks.applicability: National guidance on AI development and use. Voluntary: it defers to sectoral law (Principle 12), so for a health-data workflow it frames design expectations but cannot authorise an action.
chunks.text: The UAE emphasizes the importance of complying with international treaties and local laws in the development and use of AI.
chunks.support_note: The Charter itself defers to sectoral law. For a health workflow that means Federal Law 2/2019, not the Charter: the same deferral pattern as PDPL Article 3(e), which is why instrument resolution cannot be skipped.
